text: At the request of many people asking me to explain the Al-Tayyibat system I followed, let me first say that I
was diagnosed with stage-two cancer. It was oral cancer, and I was told it was related to smoking because
I really liked shisha and smoked it heavily. Based on what the doctors told me, I was supposed to
have part of my throat, part of my jawbone in that area, and about half of my tongue removed, so I would lose
my ability to speak. When I learned that, I was shocked, but I continued working and living my life normally.
I followed the doctors' plan: six chemotherapy sessions, and after
finishing those six sessions, I was to receive immunotherapy and then radiation. I had the first two chemotherapy sessions, then became very ill.
I developed a blood clot, and what I went through with chemotherapy made me feel that
the cancer itself had not made me feel that way. For about a month before treatment, I had been feeling relatively well, so I wondered what
was happening to me. I developed severe anemia, my hair fell out, and I started feeling very unwell. I am someone who likes to
think things through rather than simply follow whatever a doctor tells me. I felt overwhelmed and confused. In the middle of all that, I saw
Dr. Al-Awady's system. I decided to stop my chemotherapy and not continue it. At follow-up appointments, my doctor
would strongly object and tell me that what I was doing could cause the tumor to spread throughout my body. I told him I would not take more chemotherapy.
He kept prescribing chemotherapy sessions, but I refused. He then offered radiation, so I had about four or five radiation sessions and stopped.
I refused to continue radiation. The doctor said I was very stubborn and that what I was doing could harm me, and that
I was also supposed to undergo surgery afterward. At that time Dr. Al-Awady's videos were available, and I decided to take the risk
and follow his system. I faced very strong opposition from doctors and people around me, to the point that I stopped going to the hospital for follow-up because
the doctor rejected what I was doing and would argue with me whenever he saw me. The system I followed was as follows:
I completely stopped eating chicken, whether locally raised or otherwise.
I completely stopped eggs and all products made from white flour.
I did not eat regular bread or white flour products. The only bread I ate was Rich Bake brown bread.
I specifically used that Egyptian brown bread. I ate meat from sources I trusted, either
lamb or beef from a butcher I trusted. I also ate
liver, cow butter, and buffalo butter that I considered pure. If imported,
I used brands I trusted. I ate foods prepared with olive oil, pastrami, luncheon meat, and various yellow processed cheeses.
I avoided white cheese, cottage cheese, and feta, while eating
yellow or processed cheeses such as Gouda, Edam-style cheese, Roquefort, and triangle cheese.
I completely avoided white flour and products made from it, including pizza made with white flour.
In my own view, white flour was one of the main things I avoided as a cancer patient. I also avoided croissants and
white bread rolls, baked goods, and pastries. I ate rice prepared with
traditional ghee, butter, or olive oil. I completely avoided pasta of all kinds.
I also avoided leafy vegetables such as lettuce and arugula. I used parsley and celery in juice, but avoided lettuce and arugula.
I avoided grape leaves and generally did not eat leafy vegetables. For fruit, I ate grapes and figs and drank
sugar-cane juice. I also ate watermelon, but I did not eat
mango because I believed its mineral content was high. So, among the foods I avoided were pasta and
dairy products and yogurt. I avoided yogurt and cottage cheese.
I avoided eggs, milk, and white flour. I did consume sugar in limited amounts and ate foods containing sugar.
I ate Nutella and chocolate.
I also ate salmon and other sea fish, while avoiding
mullet and tilapia because I considered them farmed fish, and I also avoided shrimp, crab, and
cuttlefish for the same reason. I avoided domestically raised pigeons and said that if I ate pigeon,
I would choose free-flying pigeon. I also avoided duck and goose. I ate kofta and meat
from trusted sources, as well as liver, kidneys, hearts, and sometimes stuffed intestines.
I avoided all chicken products. As for oils, I ate fried potatoes.
I considered chips and packaged juices acceptable, but I avoided
drinks containing dairy products. I drank coffee from beans I trusted and preferred to grind them myself.
I drank espresso as well, but avoided cheap or adulterated coffee.
What else, Shaimaa? That was the system I followed. There is another important thing I want to mention.
I also ate sardines and other sea fish.
I followed this system and ate fruit such as apples, and I also ate chocolate.
I began eating sugar and these foods even though cancer patients are often warned about sugar.
I later had my first PET scan, around September of last year. After the scan, the doctor said
that another contrast study was needed. I had it, and according to what I was told, there was no detectable evidence
of cancer cells in my body at that time.
My doctor asked me to remain under observation for another six months. I was determined to continue following the system.
I said that my body showed no detectable cancer at that point. I also felt that my skin and mood had improved.
I felt my temperament, anger, and weight had improved. An important part of the system for me was fasting every Monday and Thursday.
I did that consistently, and twice a month I also fasted for about a day and a half, around 36 hours.
During those 36 hours I said I did not eat or drink. I believed this affected growth hormone levels.
I believed the level could rise greatly during fasting.
So I fasted on Mondays and Thursdays and also
twice a month for about a day and a half. I said I completely avoided food and drink during those periods, although
if I felt weak or unwell I would drink a little water or juice.
I had another test about two weeks before this recording and said that my PET scan was again clear. I sent it
to my doctor, who replied with a like. I said I had not continued the treatments and had continued with the system. On my Facebook page
I had posted that I was celebrating what I considered a complete recovery. I said I had not undergone the planned surgery or continued
chemotherapy or radiation. This is my personal experience, and I hoped other cancer patients would hear it, while also having emotional support and faith.
I believe that God created a remedy for every illness and does not wish pain and suffering for us.
I felt that God sent people into my life, and for me Dr. Diaa Al-Awady came at a time when I was
very discouraged and in pain. I continue to pray for him and to regard him as a great man.
I would tell people not to judge him only by his appearance, manner of speaking, anger, or unusual opinions. In my view, his personality helped
his message spread quickly because he provoked strong reactions and reached many people.
Others may have had similar ideas, but I felt he was the one who reached people. In discussions of awareness, I would describe this as
the 'wise madman' archetype: someone who comes to challenge reality. I believe his message was delivered, and I am grateful
to him. We are continuing after him with the Al-Tayyibat system: 'Eat from the good things We have provided for you.'
